title: Under Prabowo, Indonesia is more active than ever – but less free
gist: Prabowo's 'hyperactive' diplomacy — nearly 30 countries visited in under two years, BRICS entry, mediation offers — masks a narrowing of Indonesia's real options: a 2.9% of GDP deficit, a record-low rupiah and no alternative financier have made Beijing the economic lifeline, and the price has shown up in retreats on nickel royalties and quotas, silence on Chinese-linked environmental damage, a joint statement conceding 'overlapping claims' in Indonesia's EEZ, PLAN exercises near the Taiwan Strait, and simultaneous membership of rival AI blocs.

insights.claim: Prabowo has visited nearly 30 countries since taking office in late 2024, rivalling predecessor Jokowi's travel volume over nearly a decade, while touting himself as a mediator from Ukraine to Gaza to Iran and steering Indonesia into BRICS.
insights.so_what: Diplomatic tempo is not a proxy for policy autonomy; measure Jakarta by the concessions it makes, not the summits it attends.
insights.locator: Nearly two years into his presidency
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Successful hedging requires two assets Jakarta currently lacks — disciplined resistance to external dependence and precise diplomatic signalling — so Indonesia's foreign policy is active in motion but constrained in substance.
insights.so_what: A reusable test for any hedging state: check dependence discipline and signalling precision before crediting claimed neutrality.
insights.quote: Successful hedging demands two vital assets Jakarta currently lacks: a disciplined resistance to external dependence and precise diplomatic signalling.
insights.locator: While Indonesia continues to profess its bebasaktif doctrine
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

themes.theme: Fiscal and currency stress as the root cause

insights.claim: Indonesia's 2025 budget deficit widened to 2.9% of GDP and is projected to hold there in 2026, the country's widest non-pandemic shortfall in two decades.
insights.so_what: A 2.9% deficit sits close to Indonesia's statutory 3% ceiling — the fiscal headroom that historically anchored IDR credibility is largely spent.
insights.locator: Squeezed by ambitious spending mandates
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: The rupiah plunged to historic lows and ranks among the world's worst-performing emerging market currencies, compounding fiscal strain driven by spending mandates, weak non-extractive FDI and energy subsidy burdens worsened by Middle Eastern volatility.
insights.so_what: IDR weakness plus subsidy-linked oil sensitivity makes Indonesian assets a levered bet on both Middle East energy prices and Chinese capital continuing to arrive.
insights.locator: Compounding the crisis, the rupiah plunged
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Despite outreach to Japan, Australia, India and the UAE, no alternative partner possesses the economic size to offset Indonesia's financing shortfall, so the administration has treated Beijing as an economic lifeline.
insights.so_what: Diversification rhetoric cannot be funded; assume Chinese capital remains the marginal financier of Indonesian projects and price policy accordingly.
insights.locator: Strained trade relations and restrictive demands from Washington
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

themes.theme: Depth of the China economic dependence

insights.claim: China has been Indonesia's largest trading partner since 2013, with two-way trade surpassing US$160 billion in 2025 and accounting for more than 30% of Indonesia's total foreign trade.
insights.so_what: A 30%+ single-counterparty trade share is the concentration number that defines Jakarta's retaliation sensitivity in any dispute.
insights.locator: Prabowo’s approach reflects the sheer scale
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Since the Belt and Road Initiative launched, the China-Hong Kong bloc has risen to rival Singapore as Indonesia's top source of foreign capital, funnelling billions annually into nickel mining and processing, manufacturing and infrastructure.
insights.so_what: Chinese capital is now systemically embedded in Indonesian nickel and infrastructure — a channel through which Beijing can apply pressure without touching trade.
insights.locator: Capital flows mirror this trade dominance
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Prabowo chose Beijing for his first state visit as president, touting more than US$10 billion in bilateral deals, and Jakarta has since lobbied Beijing to bankroll the eastward Whoosh high-speed rail extension from Bandung to Surabaya and revive stalled development at the new capital Nusantara.
insights.so_what: Whoosh extension and Nusantara are the two projects whose financing decisions will reveal the real state of the Jakarta-Beijing bargain.
insights.locator: Prabowo chose Beijing for his first state visit
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Prabowo publicly celebrated the successful issuance and top ratings of Indonesia's yuan-denominated Panda Bonds in his state budget address as proof of economic resilience.
insights.so_what: Sovereign funding is migrating toward CNY issuance — a concrete de-dollarisation datapoint and a further tie binding Jakarta's balance sheet to Beijing.
insights.locator: In his recent state budget address
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

themes.theme: Costs paid at home: manufacturing and environment

insights.claim: Indonesia's labour-intensive textile and garment sectors in West and Central Java have been devastated by cheap Chinese imports, with the bankruptcy of household-name titans like Sritex and dozens of factory closures displacing hundreds of thousands of workers.
insights.so_what: Import-driven deindustrialisation plus mass layoffs is the domestic political charge building under the China relationship — a source of future policy discontinuity.
insights.locator: Consider the quiet devastation
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Rather than imposing decisive safeguard tariffs or confronting Beijing over trade distortions, Jakarta has repeatedly hesitated for fear of retaliation or alienating Chinese financiers — direct evidence that dependence has cost policy latitude.
insights.so_what: Do not expect Indonesian trade defence measures against China even amid severe domestic industrial distress; the financing channel vetoes them.
insights.locator: However, rather than imposing decisive safeguard tariffs
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Jakarta stays silent on the socio-environmental costs of Chinese-dominated nickel hubs in Central Sulawesi and North Maluku — captive coal plants, deforestation, toxic runoff and poor labour safety — fearing bilateral friction would deter future manufacturing investment.
insights.so_what: ESG risk in Indonesian nickel is structurally unpoliced by the host state; buyers with supply-chain due diligence obligations carry that exposure themselves.
insights.quote: socialising the fallout at home while shielding Chinese operators from accountability
insights.locator: Equally glaring is Jakarta’s silence
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Indonesia's recent crackdowns on illegal mining are driven primarily by state revenue recovery rather than genuine environmental remediation.
insights.so_what: Read Indonesian mining enforcement as fiscal policy, not environmental policy — it predicts royalty and levy pressure, not supply discipline on ESG grounds.
insights.locator: Indeed, Jakarta’s recent wave of crackdowns
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Under Prabowo, Jakarta tightened Jokowi's downstreaming policy with stricter mining quotas, royalty hikes and mandatory divestment rules transferring equity to Indonesian state entities, but only Chinese investors pushed back forcefully.
insights.so_what: Regulatory risk in Indonesian mining is real for all foreign investors, but only one investor bloc has the leverage to reverse it — a structural disadvantage for non-Chinese capital.
insights.locator: Under Jokowi, Indonesia initiated an ambitious downstreaming
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: In May 2026 the China Chamber of Commerce in Indonesia delivered a rare, blunt protest letter directly to Prabowo, copied to China's embassy, warning that abrupt mining quota cuts, proposed royalty hikes and aggressive enforcement threatened stalled projects and capital flight.
entities: China Chamber of Commerce in Indonesia
insights.so_what: A formal industry-to-president escalation is the observable tell that a resource-nationalist push has hit its ceiling — it preceded the policy retreat by weeks.
insights.locator: In May 2026, the China Chamber of Commerce
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Faced with the risk of widespread smelter idling, senior Indonesian ministers held emergency consultations and quietly postponed planned mineral royalty hikes while entertaining case-by-case quota adjustments.
insights.so_what: Nickel royalty and quota tightening in Indonesia is reversible under smelter pressure — supply-cut theses built on announced Indonesian policy should be heavily discounted.
insights.locator: Confronted with the risk of widespread smelter idling
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Indonesia's resource nationalism runs into structural limits against a counterpart holding deep refining technology and monopsonistic purchasing power, so the state's regulatory assertiveness met an unyielding counterpart in Beijing.
insights.so_what: Owning the ore is weak leverage when one buyer controls refining and offtake — the same logic applies to other critical-mineral producers facing Chinese midstream dominance.
insights.locator: This pushback laid bare the structural limits
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: To secure Chinese commitments for higher-value priorities such as integrated EV battery ecosystems, Prabowo established an investment acceleration task force under Presidential Decree No. 4/2026 to bypass bureaucratic gridlock and expedite licensing, while Wang Yi's August 2026 Jakarta visit called on Indonesia to provide a 'safe, stable, and favourable business environment'.
insights.so_what: Jakarta has effectively traded regulatory assertiveness for licensing speed and battery investment — bullish for project timelines, bearish for Indonesian bargaining power.
insights.quote: safe, stable, and favourable business environment
insights.locator: Eventually, pragmatic economic considerations compelled Jakarta
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Jokowi held the line on sovereignty by avoiding bilateral joint statements with Beijing on disputed waters, maintaining Indonesia's non-claimant status, rejecting the nine-dash line and asserting rights around the Natuna Islands under UNCLOS — clarity that unravelled within months of Prabowo taking office.
insights.so_what: The Jokowi-Prabowo contrast shows South China Sea legal positions are leader-dependent, not institutionalised — a source of sudden discontinuity risk.
insights.locator: While Jokowi aggressively courted Chinese capital
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: In a bilateral joint statement during Prabowo's late-2024 Beijing visit, Indonesia agreed to pursue joint maritime development in areas of 'overlapping claims', a concession that damage-control statements could not undo.
insights.so_what: A single sentence in a joint statement can transfer legal ground; watch communiqué language as the real measure of alignment shifts.
insights.quote: Jakarta handed Beijing a legal and rhetorical victory by implicitly legitimising China’s expansive maritime overreach inside Indonesia’s own exclusive economic zone.
insights.locator: In an official bilateral joint statement
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: When the PLA Navy conducted bilateral naval manoeuvres with Indonesia in the Western Pacific in August 2026, directly east of the Taiwan Strait, Jakarta downplayed them as routine passing drills without combat intent — underestimating how regional observers would read the move.
insights.so_what: Military symbolism near Taiwan is priced by observers regardless of stated intent; this is a live datapoint on Southeast Asian drift for Taiwan-contingency modelling.
insights.locator: When the People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN)
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Wang Yi's August 2026 visit produced the first-ever Indonesia-China 2+2 Joint Foreign and Defence Ministerial Dialogue, with planned outcomes including Chinese munition, rocket and missile factories in Indonesia, technology transfer and expanded exercises.
insights.so_what: Beijing is moving into the one domain where it lags Washington in Indonesia; Chinese munitions plants on Indonesian soil would be a step-change in regional defence-industrial geography.
insights.locator: Despite concerns over Indonesia’s growing closeness
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Indonesia simultaneously signed an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with the US in February 2026 and a Major Defence Cooperation Partnership, but leaks alleging a US request for standing military overflight clearance during contingencies — implicitly for a Taiwan Strait crisis — plus speculation over basing access triggered domestic backlash even after official denials.
insights.so_what: Jakarta's accommodation of Washington is as politically fragile as its accommodation of Beijing — both legs of the balancing act carry domestic detonation risk.
insights.locator: Eager to repair a rocky bilateral relationship
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Prabowo has sidelined career diplomats at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in favour of centralised top-down diplomacy, producing a cycle of hasty commitments, public outcry and awkward walk-backs that erodes Indonesia's credibility with both Washington and Beijing.
insights.so_what: Institutional hollowing raises the variance of Indonesian policy announcements — expect more reversals, and treat initial announcements as low-confidence.
insights.locator: Successful hedging requires deliberate, disciplined signalling
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

themes.theme: AI bloc entanglement as the next forced choice

insights.claim: Indonesia joined Beijing's World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation as a founding member seeking Chinese tech capital and knowledge sharing, while simultaneously staying open to the US-led Pax Silica — a straddle the author doubts Washington will tolerate.
insights.so_what: AI governance is becoming the domain where non-alignment breaks first; membership lists of WAICO versus Pax Silica are a cleaner map of digital bloc formation than trade data.
insights.locator: This vulnerability is most acute in frontier domains
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: Because Beijing treats AI as a pillar of national security and great-power rivalry, member states find it hard to resist its restrictive technical and geopolitical orbit, and Indonesia may be unable to withstand Chinese economic retaliation if China weaponises its supply chain regime.
insights.so_what: Technical standards adoption is the quiet lock-in mechanism; once Indonesian systems are built to Chinese AI standards, the exit cost rises sharply.
insights.locator: However, Beijing treats AI as a vital pillar
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao

insights.claim: By mistaking diplomatic hyperactivity for genuine independence, Indonesia risks sleepwalking into strategic subordination, with deepening economic dependence making the alignment choice by default.
insights.so_what: If Indonesia — ASEAN's anchor — drifts, Southeast Asia's collective hedging premise weakens; watch Jakarta as the bellwether for regional alignment pricing.
insights.quote: By mistaking diplomatic hyperactivity for genuine independence, Indonesia may be sleepwalking
insights.locator: Ultimately, Jakarta’s deepening economic dependence
insights.speaker: Jessica C. Liao
